theory.intro: Words like **at least**, **at most**, **not**, and **excluding** can suggest a useful complement, especially when the unacceptable arrangements are easier to count directly. The complement principle uses $\text{Acceptable} = \text{Total} - \text{Unacceptable}$.
steps: Identify the total number of unrestricted arrangements
Calculate the number of unacceptable arrangements
Subtract the unacceptable count from the total count: $\text{Acceptable} = \text{Total} - \text{Unacceptable}$

workedExamples.question_text: Six distinct books are arranged on a shelf. How many arrangements have two particular books separated by at least one other book?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total arrangements: $6!=720$.

For the unacceptable arrangements, treat the two particular books as one unit. Arrange the five units, then arrange the two books within their unit: $5!\times2!=240$.

Acceptable arrangements: $720-240=480$.

workedExamples.question_text: How many arrangements of the letters of $\text{RADIO}$ have first two positions that are not both vowels?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total arrangements: $5!=120$.

The unacceptable arrangements have vowels in both first positions. Choose these vowels in $3\times2$ ways, then arrange the remaining three letters in $3!$ ways.

Acceptable arrangements: $120-3\times2\times3!=84$.

workedExamples.question_text: Eleven students are available for four distinct relay legs. How many lineups are possible if Priya and Jack cannot both be on the team?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total lineups: ${}^{11}P_4=7920$.

For the unacceptable lineups, choose Priya's leg in four ways and Jack's leg in three ways. Fill the remaining two legs from the other nine students in ${}^{9}P_2$ ways.

Acceptable lineups: $7920-4\times3\times{}^{9}P_2=7920-864=7056$.

workedExamples.question_text: Three-letter codes are formed without repetition from the letters of $\text{ORANGES}$. How many contain $\text{O}$?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total codes: ${}^{7}P_3=210$.

The unacceptable codes omit $\text{O}$, so use only the other six letters: ${}^{6}P_3=120$.

Codes containing $\text{O}$: $210-120=90$.

workedExamples.question_text: How many arrangements of all the letters of $\text{CAMPUS}$ do not begin with $\text{C}$?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total arrangements: $6!=720$.

For arrangements beginning with $\text{C}$, fix $\text{C}$ first and arrange the other five letters: $5!=120$.

Acceptable arrangements: $720-120=600$.

workedExamples.question_text: Seven performers appear in a running order. How many orders are possible if Nia performs neither first nor last?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total orders: $7!=5040$.

The unacceptable orders put Nia first or last. These cases are disjoint, giving $2\times6!=1440$ orders.

Acceptable orders: $5040-1440=3600$.

workedExamples.question_text: Six friends stand in a line. How many arrangements are possible if neither Ella nor Finn stands at either end?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total arrangements: $6!=720$.

Ella at either end gives $2\times5!=240$ arrangements. Finn at either end also gives $240$.

Arrangements with both at the ends occur in both counts. Assign Ella and Finn to the ends in two ways, then arrange the other four friends: $2\times4!=48$.

Unacceptable arrangements: $240+240-48=432$.

Acceptable arrangements: $720-432=288$.

workedExamples.question_text: Five students and two teachers stand in a row. How many arrangements have at least three students between the teachers? All seven people are distinct.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total arrangements: $7!=5040$.

Count the unacceptable arrangements by the number of students between the teachers.

No students: treat the teachers as one unit, giving $6!\times2!=1440$.

One student: choose the student in five ways, then arrange the teacher–student–teacher unit with the four remaining students, giving $5\times5!\times2!=1200$.

Two students: order the students between the teachers in ${}^{5}P_2$ ways, then arrange this unit with the three remaining students, giving ${}^{5}P_2\times4!\times2!=960$.

These cases are disjoint. Acceptable arrangements: $5040-1440-1200-960=1440$.

foundation.question_text:
$6$ people line up for tickets.
In how many ways can they line up if Sam and Tom do not stand next to each other?
foundation.solution_text:
Total unrestricted arrangements $= 6! = 720$.
Unacceptable (Sam and Tom together) $= 5! \times 2! = 240$.
Acceptable $= 720 - 240 = 480$.

foundation.question_text: In how many ways can the $5$ letters of the word $\text{GREAT}$ be arranged so that the vowels $\text{E}$ and $\text{A}$ are not adjacent?
How many arrangements of the letters of $\text{TIGER}$ have first two positions that are not both vowels?
foundation.solution_text:
Total arrangements $= 5! = 120$.
Unacceptable (both first positions are vowels) $= 2 \times 1 \times 3! = 12$.
Acceptable $= 120 - 12 = 108$.

foundation.question_text: In how many ways can $4$ friends stand in a line if Alex and Ben do not stand together?
foundation.solution_text:
Total arrangements $= 4! = 24$.
Unacceptable (Alex and Ben together) $= 3! \times 2! = 12$.
Acceptable $= 24 - 12 = 12$.

foundation.question_text:
A committee of $3$ distinct executive roles (Chair, Secretary, Treasurer) is chosen from $8$ candidates.
If Liam and Noah refuse to serve on the committee together, how many committee assignments are possible?
foundation.solution_text:
Total committee assignments $= {^{8}P_{3}} = 8 \times 7 \times 6 = 336$.
Unacceptable (both on committee) $= {^{3}P_{2}} \times 6 = 6 \times 6 = 36$.
Acceptable $= 336 - 36 = 300$.

foundation.question_text: In how many ways can $5$ friends line up in a queue if Jessica refuses to stand at either the front or the back of the queue?
foundation.solution_text:
Total arrangements $= 5! = 120$.
Unacceptable (Jessica at front or back) $= 2 \times 4! = 48$.
Acceptable $= 120 - 48 = 72$.

foundation.question_text:
$7$ books are arranged on a shelf.
In how many ways can they be arranged so that $2$ specific novels are separated?

development.question_text:
$8$ runners compete in a race.
In how many ways can all $8$ finish if runner A does not finish immediately ahead of or behind runner B?
development.solution_text:
Total finish orders $= 8! = 40320$.
Unacceptable (A and B finish adjacent) $= 7! \times 2! = 10080$.
Acceptable $= 40320 - 10080 = 30240$.

development.question_text: Four-letter words are formed without repetition from the letters of $\text{TRIANGLE}$. How many contain $\text{T}$?
How many arrangements of the $8$ letters in $\text{FESTIVAL}$ do not begin with $\text{F}$?

$10$ athletes try out for a $4$-person relay team with $4$ distinct running legs.
If athletes X and Y cannot both be on the team, how many team lineups are possible?
development.solution_text:
Total relay lineups $= {^{10}P_{4}} = 10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 = 5040$.
Unacceptable (both X and Y on team) $= {^{4}P_{2}} \times {^{8}P_{2}} = 12 \times 56 = 672$.
Acceptable $= 5040 - 672 = 4368$.

development.question_text: In how many ways can $7$ people stand in a line if neither Person A nor Person B can stand at the ends of the line?
development.solution_text:
Total arrangements $= 7! = 5040$.
Person A at either end $= 2 \times 6! = 1440$.
Person B at either end $= 2 \times 6! = 1440$.
Both at the ends (counted twice) $= 2 \times 5! = 240$.
Unacceptable $= 1440 + 1440 - 240 = 2640$.
Acceptable $= 5040 - 2640 = 2400$.

development.question_text: In how many ways can $9$ people stand in a line if Mia and Leo do not stand together?
development.solution_text:
Total arrangements $= 9! = 362880$.
Unacceptable (Mia and Leo together) $= 8! \times 2! = 80640$.
Acceptable $= 362880 - 80640 = 282240$.

development.question_text: In how many ways can $5$ boys and $2$ girls sit in a row of $7$ chairs if the $2$ girls do not sit together?
development.solution_text:
Total seating arrangements $= 7! = 5040$.
Unacceptable (girls sit together) $= 6! \times 2! = 1440$.
Acceptable $= 5040 - 1440 = 3600$.

mastery.question_text: In how many ways can $8$ people sit in a row of $8$ chairs if neither Alice nor Bob can sit in the two leftmost chairs?
mastery.solution_text:
Total arrangements $= 8! = 40320$.
Alice in one of the two forbidden chairs $= 2 \times 7! = 10080$.
Bob in one of the two forbidden chairs $= 2 \times 7! = 10080$.
Both in the forbidden chairs (counted twice) $= 2 \times 6! = 1440$.
Unacceptable $= 10080 + 10080 - 1440 = 18720$.
Acceptable $= 40320 - 18720 = 21600$.

mastery.question_text:
$12$ members of an organisation are eligible for $5$ distinct executive seats.
If members A and B refuse to both serve in executive seats, how many seating assignments are possible?
mastery.solution_text:
Total executive assignments $= {^{12}P_{5}} = 12 \times 11 \times 10 \times 9 \times 8 = 95040$.
Unacceptable (both A and B seated) $= {^{5}P_{2}} \times {^{10}P_{3}} = 20 \times 720 = 14400$.
Acceptable $= 95040 - 14400 = 80640$.

mastery.question_text: In how many ways can $7$ students and $2$ teachers stand in a row if at least $3$ students separate the teachers?
mastery.solution_text:
Total arrangements $= 9! = 362880$.
No students between the teachers $= 8! \times 2! = 80640$.
One student between $= 7! \times 7 \times 2! = 70560$.
Two students between $= 6! \times {^{7}P_{2}} \times 2! = 60480$.
Acceptable $= 362880 - 80640 - 70560 - 60480 = 151200$.
